text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-An analyses by the Oslo Bourse shows that Norway's large industrial companies achieved good results in 1995, while small- and medium-sized concerns had a weaker year on average than in 1994.
-Metal producer Elkem ASA is considering reducing production further due to high poer prices. Elkem is Norway's second largest consumer of electricity.
-The Norwegian Bankers' Association forecasts that interest rates will fall between 0.5 and one percent.

-Danish power company Elsam is not interested in exporting power to Norway because it earns more by exporting to Sweden. Norway, hit by a lack of precipitation last winter which has left its hydropower reservoirs at extremely low levels, is dependent upon imports from Denmark and Sweden to avoid a shortfall of power next winter.
-Top Nordic business leaders, which control around 400,000 employees, predict further reductions in the workforce, a survey by Gemini Consulting and the Norwegian Business School shows.
